2609.34449.title: CORTEX: Learning to Share and Specialize in Dense Language Models
2609.34449.paper_summary: Large language models are trained on heterogeneous data mixtures, where different knowledge domains require both shared knowledge and specialization. Existing modular approaches typically impose explicit components or discover modules through interpretability analysis after training. In this work, we propose CORTEX, a learning dynamics-inspired framework that learns internal modularization within dense language models. CORTEX partitions trainable matrices into parameter groups and learns module assignments from domain-conditioned gradient and cross-domain gradient similarity. We introduce the selective lesion score and module-domain mutual information to characterize the target-domain lesion effects and alignment, and analyze how module assignment affects the trade-off between assignment bias and update magnitude. Experiments with 160M, Qwen3-8B, and Qwen3-32B backbone models show that CORTEX achieves the highest synthetic-domain exact match and largest average perplexity reduction, while remaining competitive on real-domain evaluations and forming identifiable modules.
2609.34449.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型是在異質數據混合上訓練的，其中不同的知識領域需要共享知識和專業化。現有的模組化方法通常會在訓練後強加明確的組件或通過可解釋性分析來發現模組。在這項工作中，我們提出了CORTEX，一個受學習動態啟發的框架，旨在學習密集語言模型內部的模組化。CORTEX將可訓練的矩陣劃分為參數組，並從領域條件的梯度和跨領域梯度相似性中學習模組分配。我們引入選擇性損傷分數和模組-領域互信息，以表徵目標領域的損傷效應和對齊，並分析模組分配如何影響分配偏差和更新幅度之間的權衡。對160M、Qwen3-8B和Qwen3-32B骨幹模型的實驗表明，CORTEX在合成領域的精確匹配度最高，平均困惑度降低幅度最大，同時在真實領域評估中保持競爭力並形成可識別的模組。
